items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT
COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the real property tax law, in relation to a residential and
mixed-use investment exemption program in certain cities and school districts
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6555

SPONSOR: BRESLIN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the real property tax law, in relation to a residential
and mixed-use investment exemption program in certain cities and school
districts

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To spur investment in older properties by offering a phase in of tax
increases on rehabbed buildings for a 15 year period.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1. The real property tax law is amended by adding a new section
485-v
Part 1: Defines "residential and mixed-use construction" as the
creation, modernization, rehabilitation, expansion or other improvement
of any structure containing one to four legal dwelling units with or
without one unit of commercial or retail use.

Part 2: Determines where and when this change in real property tax lax
will be administered: On or after the first day of July, two thousand
twenty-one located in a city with a population of not less than fifty
thousand and not more than fifty-one thousand, based upon the two thou-
sand ten federal census, shall be exempt from city, county and school
taxation as provided in this section.

Part 3 lays out the computation table for city, county and school
district tax exemptions, and the location where the exemption can be
accessed as follows:
Year of Exemption        Percentage of exemption
1                        100%
2                        100%
3                        100%
4                        100%
5                         75%
6                         65%
7                         55%
8                         45%
9                         35%
10                        30%
11                        25%
12                        20%
13                        15%
14                        10%
15                         5%

(b) of Part 3: No such exemption shall be granted unless:
(i) Such construction was commenced on or after the first day of July,
two thousand twenty one or such later date as may by specified by resol-
ution;
(ii)The residential real property is situated in a city with a popu-
lation of not less than fifty thousand and not more than fifty-one thou-
sand, based upon the two thousand ten federal census;
(iv) The property is located within the eligibility area, as designated
by being located within the following U.S. census tracts:
(A)_Tract_401;
(B)_Tract_402;
(C)_Tract_403;
(D)_Tract_404;
(E)_Tract_405;
(F)Tract_406;
(G)_Tract_409;
(H)_Tract_410

Part 4 and Part 5 explains that such exemption shall only be granted by
the city assessor, once an application can be reviewed.

Part 6 Explains where the provisions of this section shall apply to;
Real property containing no greater than four total units, of which one
may, contain commercial occupancy.

Part 7 and Part 8 describe how such real property tax exemption can be
ceased. Part 9 of this bill set the effective date as immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The City of Troy continues to experience significant public and private
investment in large-scale projects in the downtown area, rejuvenating
this industrial city into a vibrant place to live and work. However,
there remains a large number of apartment and mixed-use buildings in
need of repair. The Return On Investment after factoring in the tax
increase attributable to the improvement, does not in many cases, justi-
fy the investment. By offering a 15-year phase in of the tax increase,
the idea is to spur investment in areas north and south of downtown Troy
to further invigorate the city with new investors and businesses.

There is currently a statewide 485-A tax exemption available for commu-
nities that want to opt in for conversion of a commercial building to
mixed-use. It is a 12 year program with 8 years at a 100% exemption of
increase. This bill is tailored to Troy, because there are so many prop-
erties that are mixed use already, that are in need of major improve-
ments and would not be eligible for the 485-A.This bill also differs
from the 485-A program by allowing for a term of 15 years, and lowering
the 100% exemption on improvement value to 4 years.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATION:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
